meta.title: Contoso Partner Portal Published Through Microsoft Entra Application Proxy
meta.subtitle: Reference Architecture
meta.description: Partners and B2B guests reach an internal web application without any inbound firewall rule: Entra ID pre-authenticates every request, the Application Proxy service relays it down a tunnel that a connector in Azure opened outbound, and the connector signs the user in to the on-premises app with Kerberos constrained delegation over ExpressRoute. A bad actor tries the same door. Adapted from Microsoft's Entra Application Proxy architecture documentation.
meta.author: DigitalPrez, LLC
meta.revision_note: Arrows now leave the initiator (request/response flows are one-way); labels, titles and control names in Title Case; signature block fields (document id, status, reviewed/approved by). Renderer 1.2.0. Data classification on every flow.
meta.objective: Publish one internal web application to partners with pre-authentication and no inbound exposure of the corporate network.
meta.flow_summary: Partner to internal portal through Application Proxy
meta.access_summary: Partners: Entra B2B + MFA (pre-authentication). Connector: certificate-bound outbound tunnel. App: Kerberos constrained delegation. No inbound firewall rules.
assumptions: ExpressRoute private peering between the connector VNet and the Contoso data centre already exists.
Partner organisations have their own identity providers; Contoso invites them as B2B guests.
The Entra ID tenant is operated by the identity team and is out of scope here.
out_of_scope: The Entra ID tenant's internal design.
The legacy reporting module of the portal, which is being decommissioned.

steps.name: request
steps.title: A partner opens the portal's external address
steps.description: The partner's browser resolves portal-contoso.msappproxy.net, which belongs to the Entra Application Proxy service in Microsoft's cloud. Nothing at Contoso is listening on the Internet: no public IP, no inbound firewall rule, no DMZ.
details: The only public endpoint is Microsoft's
Contoso's firewall has no inbound rules for the portal
The internal URL is never exposed

steps.name: preauth
steps.title: Entra ID pre-authenticates the partner
steps.description: The proxy redirects the partner to Entra ID. As a B2B guest they authenticate at their own organisation, then Contoso's Conditional Access requires MFA and blocks risky sign-ins. Entra issues the session the proxy insists on before relaying anything.
details: B2B guest sign-in; Conditional Access requires MFA
Legacy authentication blocked
Sign-in risk from ID Protection evaluated

steps.name: attacker
steps.title: A bad actor tries the same door
steps.description: Leaked partner passwords are replayed against the Entra sign-in page; smart lockout and ID Protection throttle and block them, and MFA stops the ones that match. A request sent straight to the proxy without an Entra session is dropped: the proxy relays nothing unauthenticated.
details: Smart lockout and risk-based blocking at Entra
MFA required for every guest
Proxy forwards nothing without pre-authentication

steps.name: relay
steps.title: The proxy relays the request down the connector's outbound tunnel
steps.description: Each connector opened a TLS tunnel outbound to the service when it started, authenticated with its registration certificate. The proxy pushes the partner's request down that tunnel; the connector pulls it. The corporate side never accepts an inbound connection.
details: Connector initiates; outbound 443 only
Connector authenticates with a certificate (mTLS)
Two connectors in a group for availability

steps.name: kcd
steps.title: The connector signs the partner in with Kerberos constrained delegation
steps.description: The connector asks AD DS for a Kerberos ticket on behalf of the partner (S4U2Self, then S4U2Proxy to the portal's SPN) and presents it to IIS over ExpressRoute through the core firewall. The portal sees a normal Windows-authenticated user.
details: Resource-based constrained delegation to one SPN
ExpressRoute private peering; firewall allows 443 and 88 from the connector subnet only
No credentials stored on the connector

steps.name: data
steps.title: The portal reads and writes its database
steps.description: IIS runs the portal under a group managed service account with a least-privilege login on SQL-01. The legacy report module on the same server is out of scope and not published.
details: gMSA application pool identity
Least-privilege database role
Legacy module not published through the proxy

steps.name: denied
steps.title: There is no direct way in
steps.description: The bad actor scans Contoso's Internet address space for the portal and finds nothing: the core firewall denies all inbound traffic and the application has no public name. The only road to the portal starts at Entra ID.
details: Deny-all inbound on the core firewall
No public DNS for the internal URL
Firewall baseline change-controlled and monitored

steps.name: internal
steps.title: Employees use the internal URL
steps.description: Inside the corporate network the portal is reached directly with integrated Windows authentication; the proxy is only for people outside.
details: Integrated Windows authentication
Same application, same segment
Layer 'Internal (employee) access'

steps.name: operate
steps.title: Identity stays in sync and everything is logged
steps.description: Entra Connect synchronises identities outbound; Entra sign-in logs, Application Proxy logs, connector events, domain controller and IIS logs land in Sentinel, where analytics rules watch for credential stuffing and delegation misuse.
details: Outbound-only sync
Sign-in, proxy, connector, DC and IIS logs centralised
Analytics rules for stuffing and KCD misuse
steps.outcome: Partners reach one internal application through pre-authentication and an outbound-only connector; the corporate network accepts no inbound connection.

controls.name: Conditional Access: MFA and No Legacy Auth for B2B Guests
Entra Smart Lockout and ID Protection Risk Policies
Dedicated Hardened Connector VMs (CIS L1), Monthly Patching, No Other Roles
NSG on the Connector Subnet: No Inbound, Outbound 443 to Microsoft Only
Defender for Servers with EDR on the Connector VMs
Resource-Based Constrained Delegation Limited to the Portal SPN; Delegation Audited
Deny-All Inbound Firewall Baseline Under Change Control with Continuous Rule Monitoring

threats.title: Credential Stuffing and MFA Fatigue Against Partner Accounts
threats.description: A bot could replay leaked partner passwords at the Entra sign-in page and push-bomb the matches, exploiting weak authentication at partner organisations, giving the attacker a pre-authenticated portal session with the partner's data.

vulnerability.description: Password reuse at partners; push MFA can be fatigued where number matching is not enforced by the home tenant.

attack.scenario: Leaked credential lists replayed through rotating proxies; matches escalated to repeated push prompts.
prerequisites: Push MFA without number matching at the partner tenant

risk.consequence: An attacker holds a valid partner session and can read and change that partner's orders and documents.

residual.rationale: Conditional Access MFA (CTL-0001) stops matched passwords; smart lockout and risk policies (CTL-0002) throttle the campaign.

suggested_mitigations.text: Use cross-tenant access settings to trust and require partner-tenant MFA with number matching.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Compromised Connector Used as a Foothold into the Corporate Network
threats.description: An attacker could compromise a connector VM through an unpatched vulnerability and use its trusted path (ExpressRoute, firewall allow rules, delegation rights) to reach the application segment and AD DS.

vulnerability.description: Connector host OS or agent left unpatched; the host holds delegation rights and sits on a trusted path.

attack.scenario: A vulnerability in the connector host is exploited through the one path it exposes (its outbound tunnel responses) or through a stolen admin session; the attacker then uses the host's network position.
prerequisites: Broad firewall rules from the connector subnet

risk.consequence: Lateral movement into the application segment and possible abuse of delegation against AD DS.

residual.rationale: Hardened, single-purpose, patched hosts (CTL-0004) with no inbound exposure (CTL-0005).

projected.rationale: EDR (CTL-0006) shortens dwell time and limits what a compromised host can do.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Over-Broad Kerberos Delegation Lets the Connector Impersonate Users to Other Services
threats.description: If the connector's computer account were allowed to delegate to more than the portal's SPN, anyone controlling a connector could obtain tickets for any user to those services.

vulnerability.description: Delegation configured as unconstrained or to many SPNs instead of resource-based constrained delegation to one SPN.

assets_at_risk: Every Kerberos-protected service the delegation covers

attack.scenario: With control of a connector, request S4U2Proxy tickets for a domain admin to a delegated service.

risk.consequence: Impersonation of any user to the delegated services, up to domain compromise.

residual.rationale: Resource-based constrained delegation to a single SPN with audited changes (CTL-0007).

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Firewall Rule Drift Opens a Direct Inbound Path That Bypasses Pre-Authentication
threats.description: A troubleshooting rule or a legacy publishing rule on the core firewall could expose the portal (or its legacy report module) directly to the Internet, bypassing Entra pre-authentication.

vulnerability.description: An inbound allow rule added outside change control.

attack.scenario: Internet-wide scanners find the newly exposed port within minutes; the legacy module's NTLM endpoint is then brute-forced.
prerequisites: An inbound allow rule outside change control

risk.consequence: Partner data reachable without Entra pre-authentication; NTLM brute force against the legacy module.

residual.rationale: Deny-all baseline under change control with continuous rule monitoring (CTL-0008).

suggested_mitigations.text: Decommission the legacy report module ahead of schedule to remove the NTLM endpoint.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.
